Rekha stared at it, and something in her stomach turned. "If I win because people laughed at her, what am I captain of?" she said slowly. "Not posting."

Wednesday: A rumour went round that Charu's father had bribed a teacher. A friend asked Rekha to "just not deny it". Rekha thought aloud: "Charu and I sat together in Class 5. After this, I still want to be able to say hi to her." She told her group to stop spreading it.

Friday: At the debate, Rekha only talked about her plan for longer library hours and a science club. Charu won by nine votes. Afterwards, Charu came over and shook her hand. "Thanks for keeping it clean."

Urmila, you're worried about the student union election at your college? Let me tell you about your Binita pishi at sixteen, in our school in Kolkata.

My rival was Mitali. We had been best friends till Class 8, then drifted. During the campaign, some of my supporters found out she had failed a maths test. "Put it on a poster," they said.

I went home and sat on this very verandah. I thought: if I shame her, I am telling everyone that's how a captain behaves. And Mitali and I have walked to the tram together for years.

So I told them no. I spoke only about fixing the leaking roof over the girls' toilets and a monthly quiz.

I lost. But Mitali invited me to her wedding twenty years later, and I stood beside her. Some losses are small.

qa.q: What did Binita promise instead of attacking Mitali?
qa.a: She spoke only about fixing the leaking roof over the girls' toilets and a monthly quiz.

qa.q: How did young Binita feel about the idea of the poster?
qa.a: She felt uncomfortable and troubled by it, sensing that shaming Mitali would show a bad kind of leadership.

qa.q: Which choice in the story was the turning point, and what might have happened otherwise?
qa.a: Refusing the poster on the verandah was the turning point; had she agreed, she might have won but lost Mitali and her own sense of fairness.

qa.q: How might Mitali have felt if the poster had gone up?
qa.a: Mitali would likely have felt humiliated and betrayed by an old friend, and the friendship that lasted to her wedding might have ended.

grounding: An elder recalls deciding not to mock a rival, reasoning that a campaign of ideas protects friendships and shows the leadership being sought.
